exact_semantics_role: L2 exactness is not independently refuted. Original FPR can remain sound by declining to decide properties outside its expressiveness; the barrier is to universal totality L1 under preserved L2 soundness.

fixed_global_transition_model.name: ORIGINAL_FIXED_POINT_LOGIC_WITH_RANK
fixed_global_transition_model.semantics: Fixed-point logic with distinct rank operators rk_p for each fixed prime field. Every finite formula can mention only finitely many such operators; no input-parametrized uniform-prime rank operator is available.
fixed_global_transition_model.relation_to_R44AG: FPR repairs the fixed-field affine/GF(2) expressiveness gap of FPC.

published_theorem.title: Rank Logic is Dead, Long Live Rank Logic!
published_theorem.statement_used: Rank logics over different prime fields are incomparable; original FPR fails to capture PTIME. In particular, the uniform rank problem with the field prime as part of the input is PTIME but not expressible in original FPR.
published_theorem.successor_language: FPR* adds a uniform rank operator and is strictly more expressive than original FPR.

derived_TRUMP_barrier.claim: Original FPR cannot discharge universal L1 while preserving exact L2 semantics, despite restoring fixed-field affine solvability.
reason: Original FPR is stronger than FPC and handles fixed-field linear algebra.
The uniform rank problem is nevertheless outside original FPR while remaining polynomial-time computable.
A sound original-FPR observer can return OPEN on such inputs, but then it is not universally total.
Thus fixed-prime rank access is insufficient as a universal global decision language.

dead_zone_mapping.meaning: Failure to express the input-dependent field parameter must produce OPEN, not an incorrect decision.

successor_boundary.note: R44AH itself does not transfer its theorem to FPR*. R44AI later supplies an independent broader all-fields linear-algebraic barrier.

what_is_not_proved: L2 exact semantics is not refuted for partial original-FPR outputs.
No arbitrary-algorithm runtime lower bound is claimed.

next_admissible_math.rule: Use the independently proved broader all-finite-fields linear-algebraic barrier rather than extrapolating from original FPR.
